key_insight: A combined 3D CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict weld temperature, axial force, and defect formation in HDPE friction stir welding, enabling fast identification of defect-free process windows.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process guidelines for improving thermoplastic weld quality by tuning rotation speed, welding speed, and bottom-surface preheating to reduce force fluctuations and thermal gradients.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of FSW in HDPE
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and force histories
Process mapping across rotational speed, travel speed, and preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The CEL model matched experimental void formation and thermo-mechanical responses, while the ANNs achieved strong prediction accuracy with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99.
watch_item: The process map and ANN performance are based on the tested HDPE parameter range, so extrapolation to other polymers or wider operating conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
